x: At this point, George Coleman had a few yards' advantage over the Belgrave trio, Gregory, Churcher and McMullen—well stimulated by the exhortations of numerous "Bels" supporters.
At three miles Geoffrey Gregory was leading in 22.20 and walking in fine style. Ron Kemp was 19th, George Checkley 32nd and Gordon Waddingham 34th.
Gregory won the two miles walk, with D.
Gerry Gregory took an early lead on the uphill climb over the first mile and gradually increased it on the outward journey being followed by Barrett and Harry Churcher.
Although Harry Churcher had entered, he was unable to turn out and with Gregory and McMullen also absent we did not expect to figure in the scratch team event.

Gregory was 2nd in the 2 miles walk, but as there was only 5 entries, and one of these was disqualified in the first 100 yards, it seemed rather an empty honour, although Gregory walked quite well but was still a minute behind the winner.

The race was run over a very flat fast course and was won by a comparative newcomer, Gregory (Walton) from Mitcham's Biscoe.In the team competition we defeated our near rivals Hercules and Mitcham comvincingly.
John was second, closely followed by Manchester & Dist. Lads Club (Gregory) and Mitcham A.C.(K.Smith). This was our best start for a long time and gave every hope for a successful day.
Trevor held his place well for most of the stage and moved past Polytechnic (Beacham) near the end to take 4th position, only to be passed by Gregory (Man DLC) who had run 37 seconds faster.
BLACKPOOL - Fastest Times:--Freary (Bol)21:20 rec.,Hill (Bol)21:23,J. Jackson (NS) 21:49, Gerry North 21:59, Geoff North 22:02, Gregory (Man) 22:13.
Manchester (Gregory) and Hercules/Wimbledon (R.Holt) had closed up to within 30 seconds. At this point our supporters felt more confident of receiving second place than at anytime.
